steps.note: S1.3.1.1 states that for arbitrary initial side and central vectors a,c the eight-row schedule changes the targets by (JV+RG)x independently of a,c and restores the scratch wires, and the S1.3.1 method gives the subtract-then-undo order that makes this so.
S1.3.1.2 states the central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, that the side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one pairs, and that the self coefficient is one, as the paper does.
The plan treats only the bit case of the exchange; nowhere does it give the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 or the side cancellation at intersections zero and two.
S1.3.1.3 gives the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), with each invocation restoring its own scratch wires, matching lines 762-764.

S1.3.3.5 only says to tabulate the residuals by splitting A=B perp P and F=<t> perp t^perp, and states two rows (side 2->5 and center 3->4); the per-edge residuals and dimensions of the table (e.g. B tensor t_X^perp of dimension (a-1)(h-1), center source->1 B tensor F, scratch last->sink) are not stated.

S1.3.3.5.1 states the inclusion (B tensor F) perp (P tensor <t_X>) subset (B tensor F) perp (P tensor t_Y^perp) because t_X perp t_Y, with residual P tensor <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2, quoting line 1048.

Together these steps state that only center 3->4 decreases, losing h, that sources sum to N and sinks to Wm-N, that the signed sum telescopes to Wm-2N, and that the Ic decreasing edges add 2L for an absolute total Wm-2N+2L.

S2.1.1 states that over F_2 every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one vector, so it is nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis; it gives this implication without spelling out the paper's plane-absorption argument (which the paper adds 'for completeness').
S1.3.3.6 derives L_b/N=3*100*100/v=100/539 and S2.1.4 states L_c/N=101/539, both matching the paper.
S2.1.2 gives the weight identity, additivity of weight mod 4 on orthogonal vectors, and q_V-q_U = sum over an orthonormal residual basis of wt(v)[v.x] mod 4.

S2.1.3 states that wt(v) is odd, gives the phase i^{eps[v.x]} as (1+i^eps)/2+(1-i^eps)/2(-1)^{v.x}, and says that Hadamard conjugation turns the character into X_v, giving aI+bX_v or its inverse (the content of H diag(1,-1) H = X).

S2.1 and S2.1.4 give one kernel per residual-basis vector, s_c in all, and S2.3 (quoting line 1905) carries this to f columns as exactly s_c child calls, each one C^{tensor f} factor on one slot; this is the paper's tensored factor per residual vector.

S2.1.5 states that the zero label has frame I and the full label C^{tensor m}, and that the route from X_a carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), repaired by Z before and the scalar i^{27k} after, with the S2.1 method citing C=iZC^{-1}Z; the plan does not explicitly mention the final negation of the X outputs, beyond 'after diagonal corrections'.
The plan states L_b/N<1/2 and hence a deficit N-2L_b>0 with s_b<W_b m (S1.3.3.7.3), and L_c/N<1/2 with a positive complex deficit (S2.1.4).
S1.3.3.8 gives eta_b=339/22587335000000 exactly as in the paper.
The plan never states the complex relative deficit eta_c=73/19906842167500; S2.8 only asserts s_c/W_c <= m^sigma.

S1.3.3.8 gives the argument (deficit > 20*2^{-50}, log m<20, m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta)=s/W, so s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}), quoting line 1331 on both deficits, and S4.4.1 sets tau=sigma; the plan spells it out only for the bit case.

S1.3.4.1 states elimination with the topmost nonzero row's rightmost nonzero entry as pivot, using only lower-triangular row and column operations, giving A=E_1 Pi E_2 with exactly a ones in Pi; repetition on the active indices is implied by 'elimination' but not stated explicitly.
S1.3.4.2 states that q is chosen to avoid every denominator and diagonal numerator in the finite table of factors, so the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.
S1.3.4.3 states that a lower-triangular change costs O(V) by updating its m coordinates in descending physical order, each by a controlled shift from earlier fields.
S1.3.4.4 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, the interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j, which turns (h,d) into (h+d,d) with one interchange, for exactly a interchanges in all.
The plan names Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) (S2.9) and mentions epsilon C_1<1 (S4.4.1), but never defines E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3} or C_0=128mB^2, nor the values nu=11 and C_1=20.
The arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at internal nodes, A(e)<=8e at leaves, and the per-invocation count below E appear nowhere; S2.9 only asserts the depth bound Delta=o(p).
The plan has no unrolling B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu, no bound A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and no total below C_0 d^{C_1}.

S2.9 asserts that p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact with Delta=o(p), but it omits the defining invariant (depth-l values lie in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l) and does not derive Delta=o(p) from epsilon C_1<1, so it states the conclusion without the sub-step.
S2.10 states that every row of H=H_0^{tensor D} has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved, and that the single final truncation errs by less than sqrt2 2^{-p}.

summary: P02 is detailed on the bank exchange (bit case only), the label budget (except the full residual table), the phase interface, the bit rank saving and the matrix shear: 19 of 26 sub-steps are present and none are wrong. Missing are the complex exchange coefficients (B3), the per-edge residual table (L1), eta_c (R3), and the whole guard-width derivation of the simultaneous layer (S1-S4), where the plan only asserts Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p) and the bit reservation.
